text:
Alex: FYI ap-west1 gpu attach backlog spiking, nodes in cohort stripe-03 show huge local nvme IOPS. GPUs queued ~80s and climbing.
Maria: saw it. kubelet logs: `attach_controller: timeout` on 5 nodes. iostat snapshot: `nvme0n1 tps=280k` on two hosts.
OpsBot: ALERT ap-west1-sma: GPU_POOL_PENDING=12, attach_wait>60s :rotating_light:
Jin: this looks like scrub/janitor overlap again. We rolled scrub cadence to 2h yesterday for warmup. Any scheduled deep-scan at this window?
Maria: scrub-runner kicked at 02:06, janitor batch started 02:08, cleaner job resized, then deep-scan task launched at 02:09. timings align.
Sam: quick mitigation: can we pause janitor on stripe-03? I can patch the deployment to `replicas: 0` for that cohort for 10m. cheap and fast.
Luca: +1 for pausing janitor, but need to throttle scrub too. Lowering scrub concurrency might reduce KV cache pressure.
Alex: do it, but we need fallback for in-flight attaches. Sam, patch and also spin up 3 reserved spare nodes in ap-west1 to unblock scheduling. tradeoff: cost for immediate availability.
Sam: running: `kubectl -n infra scale deploy/janitor-stripe-03 --replicas=0`
Sam: also `repctl reserve create --region ap-west1 --size 3 --label temp-unblock` (started).
Maria: after pausing janitor I see IOPS drop on the two hot hosts to ~45k tps, attach backlog clearing. attach_wait now ~18s.
Jin: good. We should still run a targeted deep-scan on the affected disks to check for corruption without full-sweep. propose: `deepscan --nodes node-178 node-192 --level quick --no-scrub`
Alex: agree. schedule the deepscan, collect checksums, and if we see >0.5% bad sectors, plan proactive replacement.
Luca: note for postmortem: cadence change increased scrub overlap probability during high-batch windows. We should add a randomized jitter and priority levels (janitor low).
Sam: deepscan kicked. logs: `deepscan(node-178): read-error-count=0`, `node-192: checksum-mismatch=2 (remapped)`. Looks like remap succeeded, no data loss.
Maria: good catch. I'll re-enable janitor with reduced concurrency (from 8->2) and stagger start times.
Sam: janitor back to 2 replicas, stagger window set to +5m.
Alex: leaving reserve nodes up for 30m and then scale down. Cost hit small but prevented attach timeouts. Documenting: action taken, inc window, and follow-ups for scrub cadence fix.
OpsBot: Incident note created: #INC-7905550000 - nvme iops droplet causing GPU attach backlog.
Jin: follow-ups: add an alert for janitor+scrub concurrency in same cohort, and a runbook step to spin reserve nodes.
Luca: also consider adding IOPS QoS isolation for janitor tasks (nice IO) so they never saturate device.
Alex: thanks all. I'll draft postmortem and assign owners.
Maria: tl;dr: scrub overlap -> nvme IOPS spike -> gpu attaches slowed. Mitigated by pausing janitor, spinning reserved nodes, targeted deepscan, then re-enable janitor with lower concurrency.
